h1: Charoen Thani Hotel Khon Kaen — a long-standing city hotel within walking distance of Khao Niao Road
intro: Ask anyone in Khon Kaen about the big hotels in town, and Charoen Thani Hotel Khon Kaen is one of the first names that comes up. It's a 4-star city hotel with 320 rooms on Si Chan Road, and its strongest card is the location — about a 300-metre walk to Khao Niao Road and the nightlife area, and close to Central Plaza. There's an outdoor pool, a gym, free parking, and a varied breakfast that guests often praise. It's a long-serving building that shows its age in places, but the price is affordable. Rates start from around THB 1,100/night, and it scores 8.4.

body.html: What keeps Charoen Thani a default pick for visitors to Khon Kaen is a central location that puts everything within easy reach on foot. The hotel is on Si Chan Road, only about 300 metres from Khao Niao Road — Khon Kaen's well-known nightlife strip — and close to Central Plaza Khon Kaen. There are restaurants, cafés and markets to walk to all around. The location sub-score reaches 9.2, a figure few would argue with.

The hotel itself is a large building with 320 rooms and more facilities than the typical city hotel — an outdoor swimming pool, a gym, a spa, a restaurant, a bar, and free parking. Rooms come in several types, from Superior, Deluxe and Corner Room up to Junior Suite, with large beds, a fridge, a minibar and tea/coffee facilities. For self-drive travellers or groups, this scale and range of facilities at around a thousand baht is uncommon in Khon Kaen.

"Great location — an easy walk to Khao Niao Road and Central. The breakfast had plenty of variety and was tasty, and the staff were helpful. The hotel is a little dated but kept clean, and good value for a stay in town."

Breakfast is another thing reviews talk up. The buffet has both Thai and Western options, and the one travellers and Isan locals especially enjoy is kai krata — the pan-fried egg breakfast typical of the upper Northeast. Many reviews suggest choosing a rate that includes breakfast because it's good value. Staff also score well at 8.8, praised for being friendly and quick to help, while cleanliness sits at 8.6.

Now the honest part — the most common complaint is that the hotel is old and dated in places. It's a long-established building and some furnishings show their age. Reviews mention a slight water leak at the corner of an aging bathtub, not enough power sockets in the room to charge several devices, and dust in the corners of some rooms. The pool also draws comments about looking tired, and the pool bar isn't always open. This is a long-serving hotel where location and service still deliver, but renovation hasn't kept pace everywhere.

Another thing to know: being near Khao Niao Road means noise from the nightlife area. Rooms facing the road or near the bars can pick up sound on Friday and Saturday nights, so if you're a light sleeper, ask for an inner-facing or higher-floor room when booking. Overall, 8.4 from a large number of reviews is strong for the price, and almost everything dragging the score down is about the building's age rather than location or service.

Bottom line: Charoen Thani isn't a sleek new boutique. It's a large city hotel with the best location for anyone who wants to be near Khao Niao Road and Central, full facilities, and an affordable price — ideal for business travellers, conference-goers, night-outers, or groups and families. If you expect every corner to feel brand new you may be a little disappointed, but for a central base within walking distance of everything, with a pool and free parking for around a thousand baht, it's a solid pick.

A tip from following the reviews here for a while: ask for a renovated, inner-facing room when you book — the condition is clearly better and it's quieter. Pick a rate that includes breakfast, as the buffet is good value. And if you're coming during a big Khon Kaen event like the Silk Festival or the university graduation period, rooms fill fast, so book ahead and lock in a free-cancellation rate.

faqTitle: FAQ — Charoen Thani Hotel Khon Kaen

faq.q: Where is Charoen Thani Hotel Khon Kaen and what's nearby?
faq.a: It's at 260 Si Chan Road in central Khon Kaen. It's about a 300-metre walk to Khao Niao Road, the well-known nightlife strip, and close to Central Plaza Khon Kaen. The train station is around 1.3 km away, while Bueng Kaen Nakhon Lake and Khon Kaen University are a short drive, and the airport is about 15 minutes by car.

faq.q: How much does Charoen Thani Hotel cost and what rooms are there?
faq.a: Prices start at around THB 1,100/night for a Superior Room. A Deluxe runs about THB 1,300, a Corner Room around THB 1,500, and a Junior Suite around THB 2,200. Rates move with the season and city events, so compare a few platforms before booking.

faq.q: Is the hotel old, and what condition are the rooms in?
faq.a: Charoen Thani is a long-established hotel, and the building and some furnishings show their age. Reviews mention aging bathtub tiles, few power sockets, and dust in the corners of some rooms. Overall it's still kept clean and the rooms are spacious — ask for a renovated room when you book for better condition.

faq.q: Is it noisy — is it OK for light sleepers?
faq.a: The hotel is near Khao Niao Road, a nightlife area, so road-facing rooms can pick up noise on Friday and Saturday nights. If you're a light sleeper, ask for an inner-facing or higher-floor room when booking — it's clearly quieter.

faq.q: Who is Charoen Thani Hotel best for?
faq.a: It's ideal for business travellers, conference-goers, night-outers, or groups and families — within a walk of Khao Niao Road and Central, with full facilities, a pool and free parking at an affordable rate. It's less suited to those expecting a sleek, brand-new hotel in every corner.

faq.q: Does it have a pool, parking and breakfast?
faq.a: Yes — there's an outdoor swimming pool, a gym, a spa and free parking. The breakfast is a varied buffet that guests often praise, including kai krata, the upper-Northeast pan-egg breakfast · choosing a rate with breakfast is good value. Some reviews note the pool looks tired, so check the condition before swimming.
